# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 58 (Bu-Vb Pc58)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc58
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 58
**Title (English, from literature):** Not making stains on a new robe
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 58, titled *Dubbaṇṇakaraṇa* ("Not making stains on a new robe"), establishes that a monk incurs an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) if he wears a newly obtained robe without first marking or disfiguring it [Radich 2007; Horner]. In the text's origin story (*vatthu*, Vin IV 120), a group of monks traveling between Sāketa and Sāvatthī are robbed alongside wandering ascetics (*paribbājaka*); when the king's men recapture the stolen property, the monks are unable to distinguish their own robes from those of the ascetics [Bechert, Bretfeld, and Kieffer-Pülz 1997; Rosen 1959]. The rule stipulates that a new robe is one that has not yet been rendered allowable (*akatakappa*) [Hüsken 1997]. As explained in the commentary (*Samantapāsādikā* 863), making the robe allowable (*kappakaraṇa*) requires dyeing it and applying an identification mark, such as a colored smudge on one corner [Horner; Hüsken 1997].
